messages:
maya: Thinking about preemptive prefetch vs demand paging for SDK iterators. Prefetch reduces tail latency for interactive flows but complicates retries and idempotency. Thoughts?
ian: +1 on tradeoffs. Prefetch gives better UX for small, sequential reads, but if a fetch is retried you can end up applying the same page twice unless we have server-side dedupe/leases.
olga: Could be opt-in per-client. Maybe default to demand; allow client.prefetch=1 to pull one extra page.
sam: Also mobile/network cost concerns — prefetch increases bandwidth and memory usage on low-end devices.
maya: Proposal sketch: default demand; add a "light" prefetch mode (one page ahead) that relies on a lease token returned with each page. On retry, client presents nonce to server so it can safely re-serve or reject duplicates.
leah: Do we currently have any lease/nonce primitives in the API? We have continuation tokens but no lease semantics.
ian: Backend change is small: page response returns {continuation, lease_nonce, lease_ttl}. Client sends lease_nonce in subsequent ack/fetch. Server uses nonce+ttl to avoid double-advances.
olga: That will bump the API surface. We should gate this behind a capability header so old clients don't break. Something like: x-rw-features: page-lease-v1.
maya: Agreed. Capability negotiation keeps rollout safe.
sam: Edge case: partial consumption. If client fetches a prefetched page but crashes before consuming, server should reclaim lease after ttl. Clients should best-effort ack on graceful shutdown.
ian: Retry semantics: network-level retries (transport) should treat fetch as idempotent when lease is present. Without lease, we must assume potential duplication — caller needs dedupe.
olga: SDK ergonomics question: expose lease details to user or encapsulate? Hiding makes UX nicer but complicates implementation.
leah: My take: surface advanced metadata in an opt-in iterator API (Iterator.next(metadata=true)) so power users can inspect continuation/lease_nonce, but default iterator hides it.
maya: Implementation for cross-language SDKs (py/ts/go): keep same iterator abstraction with a small options bag: {prefetch: 0|1, metadata: false|true}.
ian: Transport: prefetch works well with a streaming connection (HTTP/2 or gRPC) because you can multiplex background page pulls. But streaming has proxy/compatibility issues. So support both streaming and unary paged endpoints; pick by capability and environment.
sam: We should add heuristics: if device is on cellular or memory constrained, SDK should fall back to demand paging automatically.
olga: For retries/backoff: recommend jittered exponential backoff with max delay 8s for page fetches; give clear guidance for which errors are retriable (5xx, 429, network) vs terminal (4xx client errors).
maya: Action items: (1) spec lease/nonce/ttl fields and semantics, (2) add capability header and server flag, (3) design iterator opt-in prefetch with 1-page default limit, (4) document transport fallbacks (streaming vs unary) and retry guidance.
ian: I'll add a section on failure modes (double-delivery, lease expiry race, partial consumption) and suggested server behaviors.
maya: I'll draft a short RFC with sample response and client pseudocode. Example response: 

```json
{
  "items": [ ... ],
  "continuation": "abc123",
  "lease_nonce": "n-123",
  "lease_ttl_seconds": 30
}
```

maya: And client fetch example (pseudocode):

```js
// options: prefetch=1 metadata=false
let page = await client.fetchPage({continuation});
if (options.prefetch) client.fetchPage({continuation: page.continuation});
// on retry include page.lease_nonce to make the fetch idempotent
```

ian: Include recommended backoff policy in RFC: base=200ms, factor=2, jitter=full, max=8s, max_attempts=6. Note that aggressive prefetch + aggressive retry can overload backend; include circuit breaker guidance.
deploy-bot: Staging rollout for capability flag available next week; plan: staging -> small canary -> broader canary -> prod. :rocket:
leah: Ping me once the RFC is up; I'll review for API ergonomic concerns and docs examples.
maya: Thanks all — I'll post the draft RFC in #eng-platform by EOD and tag reviewers. :heart:
